387	title: How tool calls behave
388	description: What to expect while an agent works in Frame Job. Calls run one at a time, wait for your drag, never put up a question, make one undo step each, and show in the window at once.
389	---
390	
391	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
392	
393	A tool call is one request from an AI agent connected to Frame Job, such as splitting a clip or reading the project. Every call follows the same rules, whichever client sends it. This page says what an agent can rely on, and what you'll see if you work in the window while it does.
394	
395	<AtAGlance
396	  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
397	  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
398	  tools={['undo', 'redo', 'close_project', 'import_media', 'relink_media', 'open_project', 'record_screen', 'get_media_analysis', 'split_at_shots', 'switch_by_speaker', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
399	/>
400	
401	## Edits show live
402	
403	An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the document as edited, and can be undone with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> like anything you did yourself. Frame Job doesn't need to be the active app for any of this.
404	
405	## One call at a time
406	
407	Frame Job runs one tool call at a time, across every connected client and the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/). A call that arrives while another is running waits its turn. It doesn't fail.
408	
409	So a long call holds up the ones behind it. The usual long calls are `record_screen`, which runs for as long as it records, `transcribe`, and an analysis call, which can wait up to [60 seconds](#analysis-tools-wait-60-seconds-then-resume). `export` isn't one of them: it answers straight away and works in the background. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
410	
411	A question the Assistant is waiting for you to answer doesn't hold up an MCP client, or the Assistant in another window. It's asked before the call joins the queue.
412	
413	While a long call runs, a client's request for the tool list can't reach Frame Job either. [`framejob-mcp`](/mcp/helper-and-socket/) waits 5 seconds, then answers from its own copy of the list.
414	
415	## Calls wait for your drag
416	
417	A call made while you're dragging a clip, a canvas handle or an inspector slider, in any open project, waits until you let go of the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after the drag's.
418	
419	There's no time limit on this wait. The call, and every call queued behind it, waits for as long as you hold the mouse button down.
420	
421	## A tool call never asks
422	
423	A tool call never puts up an alert or asks for a permission, so a call can't get stuck behind a question nobody can see. Where the app would stop and ask you, the call comes back with a message instead.
424	
425	| In the window, Frame Job… | A tool call… |
426	| --- | --- |
427	| Offers to convert a file with ffmpeg | Treats the offer as declined |
428	| Prompts for a system permission | Is refused, saying where to give it |
429	| Asks whether to save a project you're closing | Is refused unless it passes `discard: true` |
430	| Asks before removing a track that holds clips | Is refused, naming `with_clips: true` |
431	| Asks before a speed past ×12 drops the sound | Goes ahead, and the answer lists the clips under `audio_left_out` with an `audio_note` |
432	
433	An edit that fails comes back as a message too. The beep or alert sheet you'd get in the window never appears. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
434	
435	Anything that needs a question answered or a permission given has to be done by a person first. The rule belongs to the call, not to the app: `import_media`, `relink_media`, `open_project` and `record_screen` never ask, but if you add a file yourself while one of them runs, you still get the question.
436	
437	:::note
438	This is the rule for clients connected over MCP. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) works under rules of its own, and asks you in its tab before it calls certain tools.
439	:::
440	
441	### The ffmpeg offer is declined
442	
443	An agent's import never shows the ffmpeg question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the file is refused with the reason. If ffmpeg is installed, the message also says how to get past it. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).
444	
445	### System grants are refused, never requested
446	
447	`record_screen` never asks for the Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring grant, and never opens the picker or System Settings. A missing grant is refused, and the message names the System Settings pane. If macOS hasn't asked about the microphone or camera yet, the message says to press **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once, so that a person can give the grant from the recorder panel. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
448	
449	A Frame Job started from a terminal runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The refusal then also names the launching process and the way out: relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or give the terminal the grant.
450	
451	### Closing a project refuses rather than asks
452	
453	`close_project` won't close a project with unsaved changes, and nothing is written:
454	
455	> Interview has unsaved changes, so close_project left it open: save_project saves them, or close_project with discard: true closes it and loses them.
456	
457	Nor will it close a window with a sheet open, even with `discard: true`:
458	
459	> Interview has a sheet open on its window, so close_project left it open: finish or cancel the sheet first.
460	
461	## Which project a call acts on
462	
463	Every tool takes an optional `project`: the path of an open project, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out and the call goes to the frontmost open project, by window order, whether or not Frame Job is the active app.
464	
465	| Situation | What happens |
466	| --- | --- |
467	| The path is an open project's | The call acts on it. `~` is expanded, and different spellings of one path match. |
468	| The path names no open project | "No open project is at *path*. get_project reports the open project's path; open_project opens another." |
469	| `project` is left out and no project is open | "No project is open. Call open_project or new_project first." |
470	
471	A movie opened as a project is addressed by the movie's path. A project that has never been saved and didn't come from a file has no path, so `get_project` reports `null` and only the frontmost-project rule can reach it.
472	
473	The Assistant's calls are held to its own window's project. A `project` naming any other is refused.
474	
475	To edit inside a nest, most tools that edit also take `scope`. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
476	
477	## One call, one undo step
478	
479	Every tool that edits the project makes exactly one undo step, however many clips it touched. So `undo` takes back exactly one call, and the step's name in the **Edit** menu is the name the tool gives it, such as "Split at Shot Changes".
480	
481	`undo` and `redo` walk the same history as <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>, so they take back the last step whoever made it. Each answers the step's name, `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the project summary, and it's an error when there's nothing to walk back. Any new edit clears the redo history.
482	
483	Some tools make no step:
484	
485	- **View state:** `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` and `set_scope` change what the window shows, not the project.
486	- **Reads:** a tool that only answers, such as `get_project` or `detect_silence`, changes nothing. So does a call that made no change, which is [safe to retry](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-no-change-answer).
487	- **File writes in the graphics folder:** `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic` and `import_graphic` can't be undone, and each tool says so. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
488	
489	## Analysis tools wait 60 seconds, then resume
490	
491	Some tools need Frame Job to analyse a file first, on your Mac. A call waits at most 60 seconds for that, and the others wait behind it. What was analysed is kept in the project's cache, so calling again carries on from there and a part already analysed answers at once.
492	
493	What happens at 60 seconds depends on the tool:
494	
495	| Tool | Past 60 seconds |
496	| --- | --- |
497	| `get_media_analysis` | Refused, saying how much was covered: "The faces analysis of media 12 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." |
498	| `split_at_shots` | Refused: "The shots analysis of media 12 did not finish in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call split_at_shots again to continue." Nothing is split. |
499	| `switch_by_speaker` | The same, for the faces analysis. It only waits when one microphone is shared by two or more cameras. |
500	| `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` | Not refused. The call answers `ok: true`, an `analyzing` object and a `note`, makes no edit, and the analysis carries on without it. Call again to apply. |
501	
502	`analyzing` holds `media`, the ids still being analysed, and `covered`, the share done from 0 to 1.
503	
504	`analyze_cutout` works differently. It waits for as many seconds as its `wait` says, from 0 to 60, and answers the state it reached. It's never refused for time.
505	
506	Keep `get_media_analysis` answers small on long media. An answer over 512 KiB is refused, naming the largest `to` that fits, so read faces and subjects in `from` and `to` windows of about 2 minutes. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
507	
508	## Calls and Background render
509	
510	An MCP call counts as activity when it edits a project or moves a playhead, so it stops [Background render](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#what-stops-background-render), which starts again after its usual wait. A call that only reads, such as `get_project`, doesn't count.

520	title: "A typical session"
521	description: "The order an agent works in, from opening a project through placing, changing and checking clips to saving and exporting."
522	---
523	
524	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
525	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
526	
527	An agent works in Frame Job the way you do: bring the media in, place it, change it, look at the result, then save and export. What's different is that it can't see the window, so it reads the project for the ids it needs and renders a frame to check each step.
528	
529	<AtAGlance
530	  tools={['new_project', 'open_project', 'get_project', 'import_media', 'add_clip', 'render_frame', 'save_project', 'export', 'export_status']}
531	/>
532	
533	## Work through a session
534	
535	<Steps>
536	
537	1. **Open.** Call `open_project` with a path, or `new_project` for a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project with one track. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).
538	
539	2. **Read.** Call `get_project`. It returns the canvas, the playhead and every id. Every other tool names things by those ids.
540	
541	3. **Import.** Call `import_media` with the file's path. It returns the new `media` id and what the file holds: its kind, duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has video, sound or transparency. The file is in the project now, but not on the timeline.
542	
543	4. **Place.** Call `add_clip` with `track`, `media` and `at`. The answer lists the new clip's id under `new_clips`.
544	
545	5. **Change.** Use the edit tools. Each call is one undo step. See [All tools](/mcp/tools/).
546	
547	6. **Check.** Call `render_frame` at the moment that matters, and look at the picture. Do this before and after an edit.
548	
549	7. **Save.** Call `save_project`, with a `path` the first time. It returns once the package is on disk.
550	
551	8. **Export.** Call `export` with a `preset` and a `path`. It returns at once with an `export_id`. Then call `export_status` until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
552	
553	</Steps>
554	
555	Steps 5 and 6 are the loop. An edit that comes back `ok` says the project changed, and only a frame says it looks right. If it doesn't, `undo` takes the last step back.
556	
557	## See one from start to finish
558	
559	Here's a short session, each call with its arguments. Times are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, so `1200000` is 2 s.
560	
561	```text
562	new_project   { "path": "~/Movies/Talk.framejob" }
563	get_project   { }
564	import_media  { "path": "~/Movies/talk.mov" }
565	add_clip      { "track": 1, "media": 2, "at": 0 }
566	split         { "clips": [3], "at": 1200000 }
567	render_frame  { "t": 1200000, "max_width": 960 }
568	save_project  { }
569	export        { "preset": "h264", "path": "~/Movies/Talk.mp4" }
570	export_status { "export_id": 1 }
571	```
572	
573	`media` and `clips` here stand for the ids the earlier answers gave. Read them from each answer rather than guessing, because ids come from one number series that clips, tracks, markers and media all share. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
574	
575	`save_project` needs no `path` here because `new_project` was given one. A project made without one stays an untitled draft until the first `save_project` that names a path.
576	
577	## Follow the export
578	
579	`export` puts the job on the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) and returns. It doesn't wait for the file.
580	
581	`export_status` never waits either, so pause between calls. While the job runs, its answer has `progress`, from 0 to 1. When `status` is `done`, the answer says what the file holds, including its size in `bytes`, its settings and its loudness. `failed` and `cancelled` come with a `reason`.
582	
583	To stop a job, call `cancel_export`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
584	
585	## Good to know
586	
587	- Tools act on the frontmost project. With more than one open, pass `project`, the path `get_project` reports. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
588	- A call that can't do what it's asked comes back with the reason, and the project stays as it was. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
589	- `render_frame` and `export` differ inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/). With a nest open, `render_frame` draws the nest, but `export` still writes from the timeline.
590	- `export` replaces a file already at the path, and adds the container's extension when the path has none.
591	- `unsaved_changes` in `get_project` says whether there's anything still to save.

601	title: Units and ids
602	description: The units an agent's arguments are written in. Times in ticks, ids, track order, colours, booleans, keys that must be sent, list arguments and speed rates.
603	---
604	
605	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
606	
607	Every tool writes its arguments the same way. This page is the reference for what a number, a colour or a list means in an argument, and what happens when one is out of bounds.
608	
609	<AtAGlance
610	  tools={['get_project', 'add_track', 'move_track', 'set_canvas', 'set_transition', 'add_zoom_action', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'paste_attributes', 'copy_pieces', 'set_speed', 'add_speed_ramp']}
611	/>
612	
613	## Times in ticks
614	
615	Every time argument is in ticks, 600,000 to the second.
616	
617	| Length | Ticks |
618	| --- | --- |
619	| 1 second | 600000 |
620	| 1 minute | 36000000 |
621	| 1 frame at 24 fps | 25000 |
622	| 1 frame at 25 fps | 24000 |
623	| 1 frame at 30 fps | 20000 |
624	| 1 frame at 60 fps | 10000 |
625	
626	A time you send is rounded to the project's frame grid. Times in a `set_audio` patch, such as fades and the attack and release of ducking and the compressor, are the exception: they're lengths of sound, so they stay exactly as sent.
627	
628	What a time is measured from depends on the argument:
629	
630	- **Most times** are timeline times, from the start of the timeline. With `scope`, they're from the start of the nest.
631	- **Action times** are clip time, measured from the clip's own start. `add_action`'s `at`, `add_zoom_action`'s `at`, and `add_speed_ramp`'s `from` and `to` are examples.
632	- **Source times** are measured in the media file, played forwards. `get_media_analysis` takes its `from` and `to` this way, not snapped to the grid, and `get_cursor_events` answers in them when you ask with `media`.
633	
634	A few arguments aren't times on the timeline and take plain seconds, such as `record_screen`'s `seconds` and `analyze_cutout`'s `wait`. Each tool's table says so.
635	
636	## One id space
637	
638	Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space, so an id names one thing on its own. `get_project` lists them, and an edit's answer [names any it creates](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-landed-edit).
639	
640	An id nothing has is answered with where to look: "No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips." A number that isn't whole isn't an id.
641	
642	## Track order
643	
644	`tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack and the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front.
645	
646	A `track` argument is a track's id, not its place in the stack. The place is `index`, which `add_track` and `move_track` take: 0 is the back. Left out of `add_track`, the new track goes to the front.
647	
648	## Colour formats
649	
650	Colours are spelled differently depending on what they belong to.
651	
652	| Colour | Spelling | Example |
653	| --- | --- | --- |
654	| Clips and the canvas: text, shapes, shadows, outlines, `set_canvas`'s `background` | Four numbers `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[1, 0.35, 0.21, 1]` |
655	| A chroma key, `video.chroma.key` | Three numbers `[r, g, b]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[0, 1, 0]` |
656	| A marker's `color`, a clip's `label` | A colour name: red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple | `"red"` |
657	| A graphic's colour props | A CSS colour string, usually hex | `"#ff5a36"` |
658	
659	Three numbers where four belong, or a component out of range, is refused. Nothing is filled in or clamped. A number from 0 to 255 is the usual mistake.
660	
661	A marker's colour and a clip's label aren't checked against the six. Any other name is kept, and draws in the neutral text colour.
662	
663	A graphic's colour may also be written as `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` or a CSS colour name. Frame Job stores it as lowercase hex.
664	
665	## Boolean spellings
666	
667	A tool's boolean argument may be sent as `true` or `false`, or as the strings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. Any other string, a list or an object is refused: "discard must be true or false."
668	
669	This covers a tool's own arguments. Inside a [patch](/mcp/patches/), a boolean must be a real `true` or `false`, and so must a graphic's boolean prop.
670	
671	## Keys that must be sent even when null
672	
673	Two arguments are required even though null is a valid value, because null means something:
674	
675	| Tool | Argument | Null means |
676	| --- | --- | --- |
677	| `set_transition` | `kind` | Remove the transition |
678	| `add_zoom_action` | `region` | Zoom back out to the clip's own scale and position |
679	
680	Leaving either out is refused, so a forgotten value can't remove a transition or zoom back by accident.
681	
682	## No empty lists
683	
684	An empty list argument names nothing to act on, so it's refused by name.
685	
686	| Argument | Tools | The answer |
687	| --- | --- | --- |
688	| `clips` | Tools that act on clips, such as `set_video`, `detect_silence` and `analyze_cutout` | "clips is empty — name at least one clip." |
689	| `ranges` | `ripple_delete_ranges`, `copy_pieces` | "ranges is empty — name at least one [from, to] pair." |
690	| `groups` | `paste_attributes` | "groups is empty — name at least one of…", followed by the group names. Leave `groups` out to paste the default set. |
691	
692	Where a tool takes `clips`, a single id is accepted in place of a list. In `set_selection` an empty list means something: it selects nothing.
693	
694	A frame-rate term of 0 in `set_canvas`'s `fps` is refused too, as is a fraction: each term is a whole number from 1 to 4294967295, so 29.97 fps is `[30000, 1001]`.
695	
696	Lists inside a patch are different. `filters: []` is how you clear a filter stack. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/#how-a-patch-merges).
697	
698	## Speed rates are clamped
699	
700	Most values out of range are refused. A speed rate is different: `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` bring a `rate` outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range. A rate of zero or less is refused.
701	
702	On a clip with a speed ramp, `set_speed` scales every rate in the ramp, so the ramp keeps its shape, and the scale stops where any of those rates would pass the limits.
703	
704	Above ×12 a clip's sound is left out of the mix. The answer says so with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
705

21	
22	## Graphic clips
23	
24	A graphic clip sits on a track like any other clip, and the graphic is the clip's content. It isn't an effect you apply to another clip, and it isn't a video or image file.
25	
26	Frame Job comes with 23 [ready-made graphics](/graphics/templates/). You can also bring in a module of your own, [write one](/graphics/write-a-module/), or have [an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) write one. To put one on the timeline, see [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
27	
28	A graphic is drawn at its own size, not stretched from a fixed picture. Change that size in the [Size section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) and text and shapes redraw sharply. Scaling the clip in the **Picture** sub-tab is different: that scales the picture already drawn.
29	
30	## Modules
31	
32	A module is one file, `graphics/<name>.js`, in your project. It draws a picture, as SVG (a text format for vector drawings), for any frame Frame Job asks for.
33	
34	A module runs shut off from the outside world. It can't reach the network or the clock, and the only random numbers it can use are its own seeded ones. It also can't see the fonts installed on your Mac: graphics draw only with the fonts that come with Frame Job and the ones you [add to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/), so a project draws the same on any Mac.
35	
36	## Module names
37	
38	A module's name is its file name without `.js`, such as `lower-third` or `title-2`. A name can use lowercase letters, digits and `-`, must start with a letter or a digit, and can be up to 63 characters long.
39	
40	Frame Job skips a `.js` file in the folder with any other name, and the clip's [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/) warns about it.
41	
42	## Properties
43	
44	A module declares the properties it takes, and the inspector turns each one into a control. A property is a number, a true-or-false setting, a colour, a choice from a menu, text or a picture. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for each type's control.
45	
46	A value you don't set draws with the module's own default. Like other clip settings, properties can change over time: see [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
47	
48	## Clips sharing one module
49	
50	Many clips can be drawn by one module. Each clip keeps its own property values, its own size and its own [timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/), so one lower third module can show a different name on every clip.
51	
52	Editing the module changes every clip it draws. To change one clip's look alone, select it and choose **Duplicate as New Graphic…** in the [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/), which gives it a copy of the module to itself.
53	
54	## Same frame, same pixels
55	
56	A graphic always draws the same pixels for the same frame. What it draws depends only on the frame, the clip's size and timing, the project's canvas size and frame rate, its property values, and the fonts and pictures it uses, so the preview and an export show the same graphic. There's no clock or outside randomness to make it differ between runs.
57	
58	## Gradients don't band
59	
60	Graphics are drawn in 256 levels per colour. Where a gradient has to round to those levels, Frame Job adds a fixed, very fine pattern of less than half a level, so a dark gradient shades smoothly instead of in steps. The pattern depends only on the pixel's position, so it doesn't crawl from frame to frame. Flat colours, pictures, text and transparency are drawn exactly, and there's nothing to set.
61	
62	The pattern stays in a saved frame and in a ProRes export. A 10-bit export such as **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)** smooths most of it away but keeps the in-between shades, so the gradient stays smooth. An 8-bit H.264 or HEVC export smooths it away too, and the steps come back, so choose 10-bit or ProRes for a dark gradient. For the depth each format keeps, see [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
63	
64	## The graphics folder
65	
66	Each project keeps its graphics in a `graphics` folder inside the `.framejob` package. To see it, select a graphic clip and choose **Reveal in Finder** in the [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/).
67	
68	| In the folder | What it is |
69	| --- | --- |
70	| `<name>.js` | The modules |
71	| `fonts/` | Fonts [added to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) |
72	| `assets/` | Pictures added to the project |
73	| `history/` | [Earlier versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/) of each module, which you should leave to Frame Job |
74	| `API.md`, `API.d.ts` | The reference and its type definitions, for an editor or an agent working in the folder |
75	
76	Frame Job creates the folder the first time something is written to it, so opening a project never adds one. Every save includes the folder, autosave too.
77	
78	Changing a file in the folder isn't an edit to the project. The change takes effect at once, <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> won't undo it, and the project isn't marked as edited.
79	
80	## Graphics in an untitled project
81	
82	An unsaved project can use graphics. They're kept in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save. If that folder is empty, the save doesn't create one in the package.
83	
84	An untitled project restored from autosave gets its graphics back. Otherwise the temporary folder is removed when the window closes, so close an untitled project without saving and its graphics go with it.
85	
86	## Templates are copied in
87	
88	Inserting a [bundled template](/graphics/templates/) writes your own editable copy into the project's `graphics` folder, under a name that isn't taken. The first Lower third is `lower-third`, the next `lower-third-2`, and so on. Each insert makes a new copy, so an existing graphic is never overwritten and each copy can be edited on its own. Two copies with one title are listed under **This Project** as "Lower third — lower-third" and "Lower third — lower-third-2".
89	
90	Undo removes the clip, but not the copied file. To use one copy on several clips, [insert it from This Project](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/#insert-from-this-project), which copies nothing.
91	
92	## A graphics-only timeline
93	
94	A timeline of nothing but graphics, text, shapes and images still plays and exports. It doesn't need a video clip, and there's nothing to set.
95	
96	## Graphics in HDR projects
97	
98	In an HDR (HLG) project, graphics are drawn at HDR reference white, 203 cd/m², like titles and shapes. A white graphic matches SDR white and doesn't reach into the highlights. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
99	
100	## Limits
101	
102	- A graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
103	- A clip stores at most 64 property values.
104	- The **Properties** section shows only when all the selected clips share one module, and **Timeline** only for a single clip.
105	- A module's code has 250 ms for each frame in the preview and 2 s in an export. A frame that runs over shows a red error card in the preview and stops an export.
106	- **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** is dimmed while a nest is open.
107	- **File ▸ Delete Graphic…** won't delete a module while any clip uses it, including a clip inside a nest.
108	- Only the last 10 versions of each module are kept.
109	- Frame Job watches the first 16 module, font and picture files one by one. In a folder with more files, a change to a later one may not show straight away. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
110	- The frames Frame Job holds in memory use at most a quarter of your Mac's memory, and less when memory is short. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call, and **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens the whole reference. 136	## Try your first module
137	
138	<Steps>
139	
140	1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.
141	
142	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.
143	
144	3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
145	
146	</Steps>
147	
148	A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a valid name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.
149	
150	## The module
151	
152	A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.
153	
154	```js
155	export const meta = {
156	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
157	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
158	};
159	
160	export const schema = {
161	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
162	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
163	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
164	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
165	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
166	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
167	};
168	
169	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
170	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
171	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
172	    { clamp: true });
173	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
174	  return svg(ctx, `
175	    <g opacity="${fade}">
176	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
177	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
178	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
179	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
180	    </g>`);
181	}
182	```
183	
184	| Export | Required | What it is |
185	| --- | --- | --- |
186	| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
187	| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
188	| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |
189	
190	`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.
191	
192	`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.
193	
194	The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
195	
196	## `meta`
197	
198	Every key is optional.
199	
200	| Key | What it does |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
203	| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
204	| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
205	| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
206	| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |
207	
208	A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.
209	
210	## `ctx`
211	
212	`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.
213	
214	| Key | What it is |
215	| --- | --- |
216	| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
217	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
218	| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length plus anything trimmed from its front, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
219	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
220	| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
221	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |
222	
223	## Resolution-independent drawing
224	
225	Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.
226	
227	A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:
228	
229	```js
230	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
231	```
232	
233	On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
234	
235	## The schema
236	
237	The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.
238	
239	| Rule | Limit |
240	| --- | --- |
241	| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
242	| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
243	| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
244	| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |
245	
246	`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
247	
248	A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.
249	
250	## Prop types
251	
252	| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
253	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
254	| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
255	| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
256	| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
257	| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
258	| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
259	| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |
260	
261	- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
262	- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
263	- **`asset`.** A value of `""` stored on a clip reaches `render` as `null`, but a `default` of `""` reaches it as `""`, so test for an empty value before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.
264	
265	## Tolerant props
266	
267	`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.
268	
269	A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:
270	
271	```text
272	props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
273	```
274	
275	A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/#stale-values) for how those leftover values show in the inspector.
276	
277	## The SVG the engine draws
278	
279	Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg, an SVG renderer. It draws text with the fonts graphics can use, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.
280	
281	An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
282	
283	These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:
284	
285	| Warning | What to do |
286	| --- | --- |
287	| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
288	| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
289	| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
290	| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |
291	
292	A size mismatch warns too, but the picture still draws: `the SVG is 100×100 but the graphic is 1920×1080`. Using `svg(ctx, body)` for the root element avoids it.
293	
294	SVG that can't be read at all is an error, and starts `the SVG did not parse:`.
295	
296	## The sandbox
297	
298	A module runs in a sandbox, shut off from everything else on your Mac. A graphic can only use its `frame`, `props`, `ctx`, fonts and pictures, so the same frame with the same properties always draws the same pixels. These stop with an error:
299	
300	| In your module | The error |
301	| --- | --- |
302	| `Math.random()` | `Error: Math.random is not available; use random(seed)` |
303	| `import x from "x"` | `ReferenceError: Error resolving module 'x' from 'lower-third': imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global` |
304	| `new Function("…")` | `Error: Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code` |
305	| `eval("…")` | `ReferenceError: eval is not defined` |
306	
307	There's also no `fetch`, no file access, no clock, no `performance`, no `WebAssembly` and no `Intl`. For numbers with thousands separators, use `formatNumber`.
308	
309	`Date` is frozen. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 1 January 2000 at 00:00 UTC. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
310	
311	## Modern JavaScript
312	
313	Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`, `**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll` and `findLast`.
314	
315	## The time budget
316	
317	A runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging Frame Job, because every call has a deadline.
318	
319	| Where | Budget |
320	| --- | --- |
321	| Each frame in the preview | 250 ms |
322	| Each frame in an export | 2 s |
323	| The module's top level (the code outside `render`), when it compiles | 250 ms |
324	
325	Over the budget, you get an error such as:
326	
327	```text
328	over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError: interrupted)
329	```
330	
331	When that error gives a line and column, they're where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
332	
333	## Limits
334	
335	Each module runs in an engine of its own, with these limits:
336	
337	| Limit | Amount | Past it |
338	| --- | --- | --- |
339	| Heap | 64 MiB | An error with a line and column |
340	| Stack | 1 MiB | An error with a line and column |
341	| A graphic's side | 8192 pixels | Frame Job won't draw it |
342	| The SVG `render` returns | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) | `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most 8388608 bytes` |
343	
344	`render` must return a string that starts with `<svg`. Anything else is an error:
345	
346	| What happened | The error |
347	| --- | --- |
348	| No `return` | ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?`` |
349	| A string that isn't SVG | `render returned a string that does not start with <svg at frame 12: …` |
350	| No `render` exported | ``the module exports no `render` function`` |
351	
352	A frame that fails draws a red error card on the clip, and stops an export. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for where errors and warnings show.
353

363	title: "Edit a module"
364	description: "Change a graphic's code in any editor, see the result as soon as you save, read what went wrong, and find the versions Frame Job kept."
365	---
366	
367	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
368	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
369	
370	A module is the JavaScript file that draws a graphic. It's an ordinary file in your project, so you can edit it in any editor, and Frame Job redraws as soon as you save.
371	
372	<AtAGlance
373	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…']}
374	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Open in Editor', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder']}
375	  tools={['get_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'render_graphic', 'render_frame', 'graphic_reference']}
376	/>
377	
378	## Edit in any editor
379	
380	<Steps>
381	
382	1. Select a graphic clip and open the **Graphic** sub-tab of the **Clip** tab.
383	
384	2. Open the **Source** section and choose **Open in Editor**. The module opens in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files.
385	
386	3. Change the code and save. The preview redraws within a moment.
387	
388	</Steps>
389	
390	To use a different editor, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the same section and open the file from there.
391	
392	The file is `graphics/<name>.js` inside your `.framejob` project package, and **Reveal in Finder** takes you straight to it. Your own scripts and tools can write to that folder too, and fonts in `graphics/fonts/` and pictures in `graphics/assets/` are watched the same way. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). The folder appears the first time something is written to it.
393	
394	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, and at most 63 characters. A `.js` file with any other name is skipped, and the **Source** section lists it under **In the graphics folder**.
395	
396	To write a module from scratch, see [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) and [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
397	
398	:::caution
399	Every clip drawn by a module changes when you edit it. To change one clip's look, use [Duplicate as New Graphic…](/graphics/manage-graphics/#duplicate-as-new-graphic) first.
400	:::
401	
402	## Live reload
403	
404	Frame Job watches the graphics folder, so you never reimport anything. When a module, a font or a picture changes:
405	
406	- The paused preview redraws.
407	- The inspector updates, including a property list the module's new code changed.
408	- A playing preview picks the change up on its next frame.
409	
410	Changes are gathered over about 100 ms, so a burst of saves lands as one.
411	
412	A save isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. **Edit ▸ Undo** won't take your code back, but [kept versions](#kept-versions) will.
413	
414	## Diagnostics
415	
416	The **Source** section reports what the module says about the selected clip, grouped under headings. Its header shows the number of errors or warnings, or the module's display name when all is well, so you can read it with the section closed.
417	
418	| Heading | What's under it |
419	| --- | --- |
420	| **Compiling the module** | The compile error, or the warnings the module's top level gave. |
421	| **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** | Nothing. That frame drew cleanly. |
422	| **Checked at the clip's first frame** | What drawing that frame reported, such as a missing font or a picture that isn't in the project. |
423	| **In the graphics folder** | Files the folder scan skipped (a bad module or picture name, an empty picture, a font that loads no face) or couldn't watch. Each has a **Reveal** button. |
424	
425	Each row reads like "line 12, column 4 — message". Click the row, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor.
426	
427	Every problem is one of two kinds:
428	
429	- An **error** means nothing drew.
430	- A **warning** means the graphic drew anyway.
431	
432	The line and column are the module's own, when they're known. Some things to know when reading them:
433	
434	- For a timeout, they point at where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
435	- Some problems found while drawing name the frame in their message, such as "render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?".
436	- A warning from the module's top level, such as `asset("x")` outside `render` when `x` isn't in `graphics/assets/`, has no frame. It comes with the compile, and the module still compiles.
437	
438	**Help ▸ Graphics Reference** sets out the same rules under **Diagnostics**.
439	
440	The inspector only checks the clip's first frame. A problem that starts later shows up as the error card when the playhead reaches it.
441	
442	When the module file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are dimmed, **Revision** reads "missing", and the section shows `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`. When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, **Source** names them and asks you to select one module's clips.
443	
444	## The error card
445	
446	A graphic that fails draws an error card in its own box, in place of the graphic. The card is dark red with a 2 px bright red border and white monospaced text. You'll see it in the preview and in stills.
447	
448	It appears for:
449	
450	- a missing module
451	- a module that doesn't compile
452	- an error your code throws
453	- a frame that runs out of time, which is 250 ms in the preview
454	- a frame whose picture can't be made
455	
456	The card reads, line by line:
457	
458	```text
459	lower-third · frame 42
460	render returned undefined at frame 42 — did you forget `return`?
461	```
462	
463	Its first line is the module's name and the frame, or `lower-third · does not compile`. The message follows, then a line such as `line 7, column 3` when the position is known. The frame number is the graphic's own, counted from its first frame.
464	
465	An error card never reaches a movie. An export [stops instead](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/#when-a-graphic-fails-partway).
466	
467	## Kept versions
468	
469	Whenever Frame Job sees a module's code replaced while the project is open, it keeps the code that was there. The last 10 versions of each module are kept.
470	
471	| Code is kept when | Code isn't kept when |
472	| --- | --- |
473	| You save from your editor | The file changes while the project is closed |
474	| An agent writes the module | Something other than Frame Job removes the file |
475	| You restore a version | |
476	| You delete the module | |
477	
478	The code the module holds now is never in the list, and code kept twice is listed once.
479	
480	To go back, choose **File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…**. See [Restore Graphic Version](/graphics/manage-graphics/#restore-graphic-version).
481	
482	Kept versions live in `graphics/history/` and travel with every save. Leave that folder to Frame Job. Fonts and pictures aren't versioned.
483	
484	## API.md and API.d.ts
485	
486	Frame Job keeps two files in `graphics/` for an editor or an agent working in the folder: `API.md`, the reference, and `API.d.ts`, its TypeScript definitions.
487	
488	They never create the folder. When the folder exists, Frame Job writes them as it opens the project and each time it writes a module, replacing either file if it differs from its own copy, so any edit you make to them is lost.
489	
490	**Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens the same reference in your default Markdown app, with or without a project open.
491	
492	## How many files are watched
493	
494	Frame Job watches the graphics folder itself, its `fonts/` and `assets/` folders, and the first 16 files one by one: modules first, then fonts, then pictures, each in name order.
495	
496	That only matters in a folder with more than 16 files. An editor that saves by swapping in a new file is always seen. A save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
497	
498	## Good to know
499	
500	- In an untitled project, graphics live in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save. A file you already have open in an editor is left at the old path, so choose **Open in Editor** again after saving.
501	- Saves less than about 100 ms apart count as one, so only the code from before the burst is kept.
502	
503	## With an agent
504	
505	An agent reads a module with [`get_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#get_graphic) and writes one with [`write_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#write_graphic), or edits the folder with its own file tools. `write_graphic` compiles the code as it writes it and returns the result, so an agent sees each problem's level, message, line, column and frame straight away. A module that doesn't compile comes back as a list of problems to fix, not as a failed call. [`render_frame`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#render_frame) and [`render_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#render_graphic) show it the error card and report what went wrong.
506	
507	See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) and [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).

524	An agent is an AI tool that works in Frame Job for you, such as Claude Code connected over MCP, or the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/). You describe the graphic you want, and it can make it from start to finish: read the API, write the [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules) that draws it, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.
525	
526	Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
527	
528	<AtAGlance
529	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
530	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
531	  tools={[
532	    'graphic_reference',
533	    'write_graphic',
534	    'render_graphic',
535	    'get_graphic',
536	    'list_graphics',
537	    'insert_graphic',
538	    'add_graphic_clip',
539	    'set_graphic',

548	
549	## The loop
550	
551	<Steps>
552	
553	1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` returns it. An agent reads it once, before writing a graphic.
554	
555	2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` saves the module, compiles it and says whether that worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.
556	
557	3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.
558	
559	4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The reply to a font import gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the reply to a picture import gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
560	
561	5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
562	
563	6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.
564	
565	</Steps>
566	
567	## Read the API
568	
569	`graphic_reference` returns the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.
570	
571	No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.
572	
573	## Write a module
574	
575	`write_graphic` saves `graphics/<name>.js` in the project, compiles that exact text and reports the result. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and the file is written in one go, so nothing ever reads half of it.
576	
577	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.
578	
579	The reply says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still a normal reply, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as an `asset()` call there that names a file the folder doesn't hold.
580	
581	Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).
582	
583	[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.
584	
585	## A contact sheet
586	
587	`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.
588	
589	| Choice | What it does | Default |
590	| --- | --- | --- |
591	| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
592	| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
593	| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
594	| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
595	| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
596	| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |
597	
598	The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.
599	
600	Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.
601	
602	A frame that fails is drawn as its [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card), and the reply adds a sentence naming the frame and the problem, with its line and column when the engine has them. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.
603	
604	A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call fails before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.
605	
606	:::note
607	The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
608	:::
609	
610	## One frame's SVG
611	
612	Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` returns one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.
613	
614	It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is an error. If the frame fails, the reply says so and holds no SVG.
615	
616	## List and insert
617	
618	`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.
619	
620	Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".
621	
622	`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.
623	
624	- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The reply names the module the clip is drawn by.
625	- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
626	- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call fails with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.
627	
628	See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
629	
630	## Place a clip
631	
632	`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also place the clip inside a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.
633	
634	| Choice | Default | Limit |
635	| --- | --- | --- |
636	| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
637	| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
638	| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |
639	
640	Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed stops the call, and the error names the property. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.
641	
642	Frame Job won't place the clip when:
643	
644	- The module isn't in the folder. The error says what the folder holds.
645	- The module doesn't compile. The error gives its first problem.
646	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The error names the key.
647	- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The error names the canvas.
648	- The clip would overlap another one on the track, as for any clip.
649	
650	## Change a clip
651	
652	`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).
653	
654	- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
655	- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
656	- **In** can't be set here. It moves when you trim the clip's front, roll the cut before it or split it.
657	
658	These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.
659	
660	Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, unless the same call names one module for them all, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.
661	
662	## Read a module or the folder
663	
664	`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. The **Source** section shows you the file, revision and problems.
665	
666	With no name it reads the folder:
667	
668	- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
669	- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
670	- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
671	- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
672	- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.
673	
674	## File tools
675	
676	An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.
677	
678	| What | Where |
679	| --- | --- |
680	| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
681	| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
682	| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |
683	
684	`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.
685	
686	A module saved a moment ago can read as not compiling, with one problem saying Frame Job hasn't compiled it yet. Ask again.
687	
688	In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.
689	
690	See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.
691	
692	## Undo rules
693	
694	The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.
695	
696	| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
697	| --- | --- | --- |
698	| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
699	| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
700	| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
701	| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |
702	
703	Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again. With no clips drawn by the module, a rename makes no undo step. `import_graphic` can't be undone either, and `export_graphic` edits nothing, so it has no undo step.
704	
705	Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 versions of each module, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's code is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
706	
707	## Graphics in render frame
708	
709	`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the reply has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
710	
711	## The Assistant
712	
713	The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It already knows a graphic is a module and where to read what a module can draw, so plain words are enough. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).
714	
715	It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.
716	
717	## Related
718	
719	- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
720	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
721	- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
722	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
723	- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
724	- [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/)
725	- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
726	- [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/)
